projects.title: Projects
projects.hint: Your websites and services. Income and expenses are linked to them, as well as monitoring.
projects.name: Name
projects.inUse: Cannot delete: finance records are linked to this project
projects.aliasesHint: Names the project goes by in other sections, separated by commas: its repository (owner/name), its project in WakaTime. Time, commits and stars are found by them.

settings.title: Settings

telegram.description: Notifications about birthdays, payments and projects
telegram.notConfigured: The bot is not set up yet: the owner of the dashboard sets it here.
telegram.afterStart: Press “Start” in the bot chat that opened, then “Check”.

guide.1: In Telegram, open @BotFather, send /newbot and follow it: you get the token of your own bot.
guide.2: Paste the token into “Server key” below and save: the bot starts right away.
guide.3: Press “Connect Telegram” here, then “Start” in the chat with the bot, then “Check”.

profile.title: Profile
profile.timeZoneHint: Taken from this device by itself: reminders, due dates and the digest follow your clock.

sync.title: Sync
sync.description: Two copies of the dashboard: this computer and the server
sync.off: Sync is off: this dashboard works on its own. To keep a copy on a server and use it away from this computer, see docs/sync.md.
sync.server: This is the server. It runs the Telegram bot and background jobs; your computer syncs with it.
sync.client: This computer syncs with {{url}}. Without internet everything keeps working and syncs later.
sync.mismatch: The data here differs from the server's. "Resync everything" usually mends it:
sync.confirmResync: Walk through all data of both sides again? Everything missing on either side is sent over; it may take a few minutes.
sync.confirmDismissAll: Keep the current rows and forget all the versions that lost?
sync.kept: Brought back — it will reach the other side with the next sync
sync.parentGone: What this row belonged to no longer exists
sync.parkedTitle: Changes that could not be applied

backup.title: Backups
backup.latestCopy: Latest copy of the server's backup here: {{time}}, {{size}} MB ({{count}} kept)
backup.restoreOk: Test restore {{time}}: {{tables}} tables, {{rows}} rows — all in place
backup.restoreMismatch: The test restore lost rows in {{table}}: {{restored}} of {{live}}
backup.copied: The backup copy is up to date

server.missing: No dumps yet — is the backup container running?
server.stale: The newest dump is more than a day old — is the backup container running?
server.unchecked: No test restore for more than a week.
server.restore-failed: The latest test restore did not go well.

client.missing: No copy of the server's backup on this computer yet.
client.stale: The newest copy here is several days old.
client.unchecked: The server has not test-restored a dump for more than a week.
client.restore-failed: The server's latest test restore did not go well.

security.title: Security
security.off: Off: signing in needs only the password.
security.scan: Scan the QR code with an authenticator app (Google Authenticator, 1Password, Aegis…) and enter the code it shows.
security.manual: Or enter the key by hand:
security.codesHint: Recovery codes: each signs in once when your phone is not at hand. Save them somewhere safe — they are shown only now.

data.title: Export and import
data.subtitle: Everything you keep here as one file
data.exportHint: A ZIP with all your records (JSON), the transactions as CSV, the diary as Markdown and the photos. Passwords and the tokens of integrations are never in it.
data.preview: The archive of {{date}} would add {{added}} records; {{existing}} are here already and stay as they are.
data.applied: Added {{added}} records from the archive of {{date}}; {{existing}} were here already.
data.unknown: Left out — this dashboard has no such sections: {{tables}}
data.notArchive: This is not an archive of a dashboard, or it is damaged.
data.otherAccount: This archive is already imported into another account of this dashboard.
data.gone: The uploaded archive is gone: pick the file again.
data.failed: It did not work. Nothing was changed.

trash.title: Trash
trash.subtitle: Deleted in the last 30 days — by you or by the AI assistant
trash.confirmForever: Delete this for good? It cannot be restored then.
trash.parentFirst: Restore what it belonged to first (for example, the project)

settings.integrationsIntro: Connections to outside services: where the modules take their data from, which AI answers. Grey — what can be connected but is not.
settings.notificationsIntro: Where the dashboard's messages come (Telegram, the phone), when they keep quiet, and what was sent.
settings.devicesIntro: What the phone and the computers do for the dashboard. The settings are the same on every device; the ones of one kind of device are marked with its colour.

phone.title: Only for the phone
phone.elsewhere: it is set in the Android app; here you see its state

desktop.title: Only for the computer
desktop.elsewhere: it is set in the desktop app; here you see its state

system.jobsHint: What runs by itself and how its last run went

system.logHint: What the server wrote in the last 14 days; an error also comes as a notification
system.logEmpty: Nothing here — the server has no complaints.

theme.black: Black background in the dark mode (for OLED screens)
theme.glow: Glow of the accent colours behind the page
theme.own: This device has a look of its own.
theme.shared: This device shows the look of the account.
theme.builtIn: This device shows the built-in look.
theme.devicesHint: Changes of the theme, the sections and the home page stay on this device. “Apply everywhere” makes them the look of the account: every device takes it, their own included.
theme.useAccount: Back to the look of the account
theme.notApplied: Could not save. Please try again.

sections.title: Sections
sections.hint: A hidden section leaves the menu and the home page. Its data keeps coming and the assistant still sees it.

deviceBackup.title: Copies on the computer
deviceBackup.elsewhere: The desktop app keeps a copy of your data on its computer every day. Install it in Settings → Apps.
deviceBackup.subtitle: Your data kept here too, in case the server is gone
deviceBackup.latest: The latest copy: {{date}}, {{size}} MB. Copies kept: {{count}}.
deviceBackup.none: No copy yet: the first one is made within a minute of the start, then once a day.
deviceBackup.hint: Once a day the app saves the archive of “Export everything” here. The server gone or not paid for, the data stays: put the archive back through “Import archive” into any dashboard. The archive is not encrypted (the medical texts too) — keep the folder private, or choose an encrypted drive.

desktop.title: Desktop app
desktop.about: A tray app for Windows, macOS and Linux: native notifications, time at the computer, focus sessions, quick capture, copies of your data on the disk — and it keeps the browser extension up to date.
desktop.updates: It updates itself from this server every 2 hours, with no installer: a new installer is needed only for a new Electron (the tray says so).

extension.title: Browser extension
extension.about: The password vault in Chrome, Edge or Brave: fills logins, offers to save new ones, makes strong passwords. Encrypted on the device with your master password.

withDesktop.folder: The desktop app keeps the extension in this folder:
withDesktop.updates: It updates itself: the app brings every new version into the folder, and the extension reloads with it (you unlock the vault again after an update).

extension.chrome: Open chrome://extensions and switch on Developer mode (top right).
extension.loadFolder: Press "Load unpacked" and choose that folder. Then sign in to the extension with this dashboard's address.
extension.unzip: Unzip it into a folder that stays (not Downloads).
extension.notOnServer: This server has no extension to hand out (it runs from the sources).
extension.withoutDesktop: Without the desktop app the extension does not update itself: it says when a new version is out, and you load the new zip the same way. With the desktop app on this computer, load it from the app's folder instead (Settings → Apps inside the app) — then it updates by itself.

mobile.title: Mobile app
mobile.about: Android: the dashboard on the phone, which works without a network too. Later it collects what the phone and a band know — sleep, stress, time in apps.
mobile.notOnServer: This server has no Android app to hand out yet: it comes with the next deploy.
mobile.openOnPhone: Open this page on the phone and download the app.
mobile.allowInstall: Open the downloaded file; Android asks to allow installing apps from the browser — allow it once.
mobile.connect: Start the app and enter this dashboard's address.
mobile.updates: The interface updates itself from this server after every deploy; a new download is needed only when the app itself changes (this card says so).

devices.title: My devices
devices.subtitle: Where the apps run, and whether the newest version has come there
devices.forget: Forget the device (it comes back when its app reports again)
devices.none: No device has reported yet: an app reports itself a minute after it starts.

deliveries.hint: The latest notifications and what became of them. A failed one is tried again; the same one within a few minutes goes out once.

statuses.held: Waits for the end of quiet hours

clients.claudeCode: Claude Code (a command in the terminal)

push.title: Push on the phone
push.description: Notifications in the Android app, next to Telegram
push.notConfigured: Not set up yet: the owner of the dashboard sets the Firebase key here.
push.noPhones: No phone takes them yet: open this page in the Android app and switch them on.

phone.denied: Android does not allow notifications for the app: allow them in the phone settings → Apps → Personal Dashboard → Notifications.
phone.unavailable: This phone cannot take them yet: the app needs the version built with Firebase (Settings → Apps).

push.testSent: Test notification sent to the phone
push.testFailed: Could not send: see the Firebase key and the phone

guide.1: Open the Firebase console and add a project (Google Analytics is not needed).
guide.2: Project settings → General → “Add app” → Android, package name com.personalworld.dashboard. Download google-services.json and put it into the deploy folder of the project on your computer: deploy.sh builds the app with it.
guide.3: Project settings → Service accounts → “Generate new private key”: a JSON file is downloaded.
guide.4: Open that file, copy all of it into “Server key” below and save: the server checks it with Firebase.
guide.5: Deploy, install the new version of the app on the phone (Settings → Apps) and allow notifications when it asks.

calm.title: A gentle mode
calm.hint: For hard evenings and nights: fewer things that push
calm.quietHint: Telegram and the phone keep quiet in them; what came meanwhile arrives at their end as one message. A test you send yourself still comes.
calm.softOverdueHint: A task past its date is not shown in red and is not named in the morning digest. It stays in the list as it is.

phone.title: The phone as a sensor
phone.hint: Time in apps, their notifications and the places of the day, to Activity — for the dashboard to see what takes the day

steps.location: Location, all the time (places and trips; a low-power fix every 15 minutes)
steps.unrestricted: No battery limits in the background
steps.autostart: Autostart (MIUI: switch it on for Personal Dashboard)

phone.where: The time in apps comes to Activity as this phone, the notifications to Activity → Notifications, the places to Activity → Places, every 15 minutes.
phone.update: This version of the app cannot collect yet: install the new one over it, then come back here.
phone.checking: Checking what this phone can do…
phone.noPhones: No phone collects yet. Install the Android app (Settings → Apps) and switch it on in it: Settings → Devices.
